definitions.explanation: In soccer, the technique of moving while maintaining control of the ball with the feet. In basketball, bouncing the ball while moving.

examples.japanese: ⟦{華麗|かれい}→華麗：09199_karei⟧なドリブル⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}いた→抜く：02384_nuku⟧。
examples.english: He dribbled past the opponent with elegant skill.

examples.japanese: ドリブル⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{技術|ぎじゅつ}→技術：01389_gijutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{磨|みが}く→磨く：02427_migaku⟧。
ドリブル⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{突破|とっぱ}→突破：13755_toppa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{試|こころ}みた→試みる：01943_kokoromiru⟧。
examples.english: He attempted to break through by dribbling.

notes:
ドリブル is borrowed from English "dribble" and is common in sports commentary and everyday sports talk.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ドリブル⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}く→抜く：02384_nuku⟧: to dribble past someone
- ドリブル⟦{突破|とっぱ}→突破：13755_toppa⟧: dribbling breakthrough
- ドリブル⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上手|うま}い→上手い：01279_umai⟧: to be good at dribbling
- ドリブル⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{仕掛|しか}ける→仕掛ける：04243_shikakeru⟧: to make a move while dribbling

SOCCER vs BASKETBALL:
- Soccer: controlling the ball with the feet while moving forward
- Basketball: bouncing the ball while moving

In Japanese sports vocabulary, ドリブル is used the same way in both sports. Context (⟦サッカー→サッカー：04726_sakkaa⟧ or ⟦バスケ→バスケ：06773_basuke⟧) clarifies which sport is meant.
